title: Eksamensoverblik og forberedelsesguide
body:
# Eksamensoverblik – 62133, Fall 2026

## Den beskrevne prøve

Kilde: kursets Exam-side og regnearket “12 temaer plus ting i kan vælge at komme ind på i jeres 5 min”.

Du trækker ét af 12 temaer, ikke et konkret spørgsmål. Du holder en fem minutters præsentation ved tavlen og vælger selv din vinkel inden for temaet. Derefter stiller underviser og censor spørgsmål: først til præsentationen, dernæst til resten af temaet og også til andre dele af pensum. Prøven varer 20 minutter inklusive votering, karakter og kort feedback.

Du må medbringe ét A4-ark pr. tema. Når du har trukket, har du 60 sekunder til at orientere dig i det tilhørende ark. Derefter må du ikke se i det igen. Underviseren anbefaler, at du bruger tiden på at skrive din på forhånd forberedte agenda på tavlen, gerne fem-seks linjer.

Konsekvensen for forberedelsen: Det er utilstrækkeligt kun at kunne læse en god forklaring op. Du skal kunne tegne, forklare og bruge den uden papiret, og kunne svare uden for din valgte femminutters vinkel.

## De 12 temaer

Eksemplerne nedenfor følger underviserens forslag. De er mulige vinkler, ikke en udtømmende afgrænsning af pensum.

| Nr. | Tema | Forslag fra eksamensarket |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Strategic fit | Zone of strategic fit, implied uncertainty og forskellige aktørers roller i kæden. |
| 2 | Supply chain drivers and metrics | DuPont og ROA: fabrik i Kina kontra transport fra Europa; større sikkerhedslager; framework for supply chain decisions. |
| 3 | Distribution network design | Manufacturer storage/direct shipping kontra distributor storage/last-mile delivery; valg af netværk; antal faciliteter og konsekvenser for tid, lager og transport. |
| 4 | Network design | Framework for network design decisions; gravity-modellen; faktorer bag netværksvalg; capacitated plant location. |
| 5 | Location decisions | Locational break-even, factor rating og center-of-gravity fra det supplerende kapitel. |
| 6 | Cycle inventory | Fælles bestilling/levering, aggregering med kapacitetsbegrænsning, all-unit kontra marginal quantity discounts og design af rabatter. |
| 7 | Safety inventory | Sikkerhedslager ved ønsket CSL; CSL, fill rate og order fill rate; continuous og periodic review. |
| 8 | Product availability | Over- og understocking; optimal servicegrad for sæsonvarer. Eksemplet i femminuttersforslaget skal ikke medtage expected-profit-beregningen. |
| 9 | Transportation and transport modelling | Direct shipping kontra milk runs; stepping-stone-metoden; TL og LTL med Faulkswagon som eksempel. |
| 10 | Supply chain coordination | Informationsdeling og bullwhip; VMI og CRP. |
| 11 | Sustainability and circular supply chains | Revenue streams i reverse supply chains; cradle-to-cradle; CopyMagic; reverse logistics og de syv “deadly sins”. |
| 12 | Remanufacturing | Definition; kobling til circular SC; egen workshop (produkt, track, handling, læring). Faulkswagen er tværgående case — ikke tema 12. |

## Forslag til arbejdsform

1. Lav en kort forklaring af hvert temas centrale problem: Hvilken beslutning hjælper teorien med at tage?
2. Vælg én femminutters vinkel fra hvert tema. Skriv fem-seks punkter og vælg én central figur, beregning eller case.
3. Løs de tilhørende øvelser uden løsningsarket. Forklar variabler, enheder, antagelser og resultatets betydning højt.
4. Besvar spørgsmålene i de relevante 4xExplanation-ark. De er gode til at opdage huller uden for din præsentation.
5. Træn med præcis 60 sekunders kig og fem minutters tavleforklaring. Øv derefter spørgsmål fra både samme og andre temaer.

En nyttig skabelon til hvert A4-ark er: agenda → problem → figur/model → lille eksempel → vigtig afvejning → antagelser og begrænsninger. Arket er en hukommelsesstøtte før præsentationen, ikke et manuskript, du kan bruge undervejs.

## Faglige skel vi bør teste mundtligt

Dette er forslag til træning baseret på emnerne i materialet, ikke nye eksamenskrav.

- **Strategic fit:** Kan du skelne efterspørgselsusikkerhed fra den usikkerhed, kundeløftet pålægger kæden, og begrunde behovet for responsiveness?
- **DuPont:** Kan du følge en beslutning gennem både resultat og kapitalbinding, frem for automatisk at kalde mere lager godt eller dårligt?
- **Last-mile delivery:** Det er sidste transportled frem til kunden, fx fra et lokalt distributionslager til kundens adresse. Kort leveringstid kan kræve flere lokale lagre og dyrere distribution. Skeln den konkrete netværksmodel i pensum fra udtrykket “last mile” generelt.
- **Netværk og lokalisering:** Kan du skelne valg af faciliteter og kapacitet fra fordeling af leverancer mellem allerede givne faciliteter?
- **Gravity-modeller:** Brug den konkrete models formål og omkostnings-/afstandsfunktion. Antag ikke, at et simpelt vægtet koordinatgennemsnit og bogens iterative gravity-model altid giver samme løsning.
- **Cycle inventory:** Kan du forklare, hvorfor større partier reducerer antal bestillinger, men øger gennemsnitslageret, og hvorfor en lavere stykpris ikke alene afgør rabatvalget?
- **Safety inventory:** CSL tæller cyklusser uden stockout; fill rate tæller den andel af efterspørgslen, der dækkes fra lager; order fill rate handler om komplette ordrer. De er ikke udskiftelige procenter.
- **Product availability:** Kan du forklare, hvorfor omkostningen ved én enhed for lidt skal afvejes mod én enhed for meget? Fravalget af expected profits i ét præsentationsforslag er ikke dokumentation for, at beregningen er fjernet fra hele pensum.
- **Transportation:** Kan du forklare ændringer i både transport- og lageromkostninger ved TL, LTL, milk runs og aggregering?
- **Coordination:** Kan du vise, hvordan lokale beslutninger og informationsforsinkelse skaber variation op gennem kæden, også uden tilsvarende variation i slutkundernes køb?
- **Circular supply chains:** Kan du skelne repair, refurbishing, remanufacturing, cannibalization og recycling, og forklare både indtægter og omkostninger ved en returløsning?
- **Faulkswagon:** Kan du udfordre en brugbar startløsning? Refleksionssliden peger bl.a. på flere/mindre fabrikker, flere DW'er, bedre kapacitetsallokering og direkte TL til store CREP'er. Hvert forslag har følgevirkninger for andre omkostninger og service.

## Materiale at prioritere først

Start med eksamensarket, de relevante forelæsningsslides og 4xExplanation-spørgsmålene. Brug dernæst opgaver og løsninger til at teste anvendelse. Til lokalisering og stepping stone skal du også bruge de supplerende kapitler. Til cirkulære forsyningskæder skal du bruge artiklerne, ikke kun slides. Bevar Faulkswagon som et gennemgående eksempel, der forbinder placering, kapacitet, transport, lager og service.

Walmart-teksten er med i pakken. Introduktionssliden beskriver den som ikke direkte eksamenspensum, men som et nyttigt eksempel i præsentationer.

title: Strategic fit — hvad du skal kunne forklare
body:
Strategic fit betyder, at virksomhedens competitive strategy (hvad kunden prioriterer) er konsistent med supply chain strategy (hvordan kæden leverer det).

**Tre krav til fit (Chopra):**
1. Forstå kundebehov og usikkerhed i supply/demand.
2. Forstå supply chain-capabilities på spektret effektiv ↔ responsiv.
3. Match SC-responsiveness med implied demand uncertainty (IDU).

**Demand uncertainty vs IDU:** Demand uncertainty er den statistiske variation i efterspørgslen. IDU er den usikkerhed kæden reelt skal håndtere, når du også tager højde for lead time, servicegrad, variety, innovation og customization. Samme marked kan have forskellig IDU afhængigt af hvad I lover kunden.

**Fig. 2-5 Zone of strategic fit:** X = implied uncertainty, Y = responsiveness. Høj IDU kræver høj responsiveness. Under zonen: stockouts og tabt salg. Over zonen: unødvendigt dyrt.

**Fig. 2-3 Cost-Responsiveness Efficiency Frontier:** Du kan ikke bare være “både billigst og hurtigst” uden trade-off — frontier’en viser den effektive grænse mellem cost og responsiveness.

**Fig. 2-4 Responsiveness Spectrum:** Fra meget effektiv til meget responsiv. Drivers (tema 2) flytter dig langs spektret.

**Fisher (1997):** Funktionelle produkter (forudsigelig efterspørgsel) → efficient SC. Innovative produkter (uforudsigelig efterspørgsel) → responsive SC. Mismatch koster.

**Walmart som eksempel (ikke direkte pensum, men godt i præsentation):** Se “Samuel’s Top 5” — inventory replaced by information, logistics tech, standards, total cost, koordinering af usikker supply/demand.

title: Walmart / Samuel’s Top 5 — vigtige træk
body:
Supply Chaining – From ”The World is Flat” by Thomas Friedman 
 
Important characteristics (top 5 in bold text) 
1. Logistics technology (scanners, trucks, trailers, docks, conveyor belts, IT e.g. Pick-by-voice system in 
distribution centers) 
2. Replacing inventory with information – Real time information sharing from retail to warehouse to 
supplier. E.g. whether sales of yellow sweaters is lower than sales of red sweaters. (“Retail Link 
Private Extranet”) 
3. Common standards between firms (pallet sizes, information on receipts, packaging techniques, etc.) 
4. Focus on total cost of delivering 
5. Coordinating disruption-prone supply with hard-to-predict demand (forecasting techniques) 
6. “Visibility” into where products are 
7. Using “Postponement” to reduce the time from idea to delivered product 
8. Building up products from standard parts in many configurations minimizes obsolete parts/products 
(technically that’s DELL and not Walmart) 
9. Having vendors physically around in “Vendorville” in Bentonville 
10. Buying goods in volume directly from manufacturers yielding low prices 
11. A central distribution center with own fleet of trucks supplying the stores 
12. Rerouting empty trucks to new pick-ups using GPS technology 
13. Using Pick-by-voice in warehouses   
14. Constant focus on improvement of physical supply chain and information to manufacturers 
15. Low cost culture 
16. Learning customers buying patterns leads to low inventories 
17. Sharing sales data with suppliers and CPFR (Collaborative planning, forecasting and replenishment) 
18. Use of RFID technology to log information about sales and much more 
19. Every-day-low-price (easier to forecast sales) 
The internal Wal-Mart supply chain is a distribution supply chain. The chapter also describes external issues, 
e.g. the way the company relates to their suppliers and customers in the network.

title: Customer priorities, DuPont og drivers
source: Strategy, Finance and Supply Chain (slides) + Chopra
body:
**Customer priorities (Slack & Lewis):** Quality, Speed, Dependability, Flexibility, Cost.
En virksomhed konkurrerer typisk på få af dem — ofte lav pris ELLER en kombination af de øvrige. I Chopra samles det i Efficiency vs Responsiveness.

**DuPont / ROA:**
ROA = Net profit margin × Asset turnover
- Margin = Net profit / Sales
- Turnover = Sales / Total assets
- Assets = current + fixed

Supply chain påvirker begge sider: COGS, transport, holding (margin) og inventory, anlæg, tilgodehavender (assets).

**Case 1 — fabrik i Kina i stedet for eksport:** Fixed assets stiger (turnover falder). Unit cost/transport til Kina-markedet kan forbedre margin. ROA afgøres af nettoeffekten — fortæl begge sider.

**Case 2 — fordoblet færdigvarelager:** Current assets stiger (turnover falder), holding costs stiger. Færre empty shelves kan øge sales. Kort sigt ofte ROA↓ hvis sales-løftet ikke kompenserer.

**Seks drivers:** Facilities, Inventory, Transportation (logistiske) + Information, Sourcing, Pricing (cross-functional). Hver kan designes mere effektiv eller mere responsiv.

title: De seks distributionsarketyper
body:
Chopra præsenterer seks arketyper for flow fra fabrik til kunde:

1. **Manufacturer storage with direct shipping** (dropshipping)
2. **Manufacturer storage with direct shipping and in-transit merge**
3. **Distributor storage with carrier delivery**
4. **Distributor storage with last-mile delivery**
5. **Manufacturer/distributor storage with customer pick-up**
6. **Retail storage with customer pick-up**

**Øvelseskrav:** Vælg én blandt #1–3 og én blandt #4–6. Vurder dem på:
- Inventory costs
- Transport costs
- Response time
- Product variety

**Nøglebegreber fra øvelsen:**
- Aggregation = samle lager på færre lokationer længere upstream → mere TL, lavere inventory, længere RT.
- Disaggregation = sprede lager downstream → mere LTL, kortere RT, højere inventory.
- TL (truckload) mellem factory og DC er relativt billigt.
- LTL (less-than-truckload) tættere på kunde er dyrere.

**8. udgave-advarsel:** Arketyperne er skåret ned til ca. 1½ side. Brug de uploadede ~16 sider fra 7. udgave på DTU Learn.

title: Cycle inventory — teori til at læse
body:
**Hvorfor cycle inventory?** Fordi fixed ordering/setup/transport costs gør det dyrt at bestille én ad gangen. Cycle inventory = Q/2 ved jævnt forbrug.

**EOQ (purchasing):** Q* = √(2DS / hC)
- D = årlig efterspørgsel
- S = fixed order cost pr. ordre
- C = cost pr. enhed
- h = holding cost rate (andel af C pr. år)
Holding cost pr. enhed pr. år = hC.

**Production lot size** adskiller sig fra purchasing, fordi produktion foregår med en rate P > D, så lager bygges op med (1 − D/P).

**Ordering costs (fire typiske):** buyer time, transportation fixed, receiving/inspection, admin/other.

**Holding costs (fem typiske):** capital, storage, obsolescence, insurance/tax, handling/pilferage m.m. (følg bogens liste).

**All-unit quantity discount:** Hele ordren får den lavere pris, når Q overstiger cutoff.
**Marginal (incremental) quantity discount:** Kun enheder over cutoff får den lavere pris.

**Aggregation / joint ordering:** Del fixed cost S mellem flere produkter → mindre Q pr. produkt. Kapacitetsbegrænsning (truck) kan begrænse gevinsten (Ex 11-4 / 11-5).

title: Safety inventory — læsestof
body:
Safety inventory er buffer mod usikkerhed i demand/supply over lead time.

**Tre spørgsmål:** Hvilket availability-niveau? Hvor meget ss? Hvordan sænke ss uden at miste service?

**Service metrics:**
- **CSL (Cycle Service Level):** P(ingen stockout i en replenishment-cyklus)
- **Fill rate:** andel af efterspurgte enheder leveret fra lager
- **Order fill rate:** andel komplette ordrer

De er ikke udskiftelige procenter.

**Formel:** ss = z · σ_L  (σ_L = std.afv. for lead-time demand)
**Continuous review:** ROP = D·L + ss
**Periodic review:** skal dække lead time + review interval → typisk mere ss.

**Sænk ss via:** kortere LT, bedre forecast, risk pooling/aggregation, information sharing (link til coordination).

title: Product availability / Newsvendor — læsestof
body:
Bruges til one-shot / sæson (fashion, elektronik, julevarer) — ikke samme logik som løbende safety stock.

**Co** = cost of overstocking = c − s  (indkøb minus salvage)
**Cu** = cost of understocking = p − c  (mistet margin)

**Optimal CSL*** = Cu / (Cu + Co)
**Q*** = F⁻¹(CSL*)

Højere salvage → lavere Co → højere CSL*. Høj Cu (dyrt at mangle) → højere service.

Eksamensvinkel: forklar Co/Cu med tal, find CSL*, fortæl betydningen. Expected-profit-beregning behøver ikke med i 5-min-forslaget, men kan komme i dialogen.

title: Transportation — Chopra + TL/LTL/milk runs
body:
**Direct shipping vs milk runs (Ex 14-1):** Høj demand → direct ofte bedst. Lav demand → milk runs kan vinde, fordi inventory/lot-size-effekter og stop-deling ændrer total cost.

**TL vs LTL:** TL = fuld lastbil, lav cost/enhed, godt factory→DW. LTL = delt last, dyrere, flere stop — typisk DW→kunde/CREP.

**Faulkswagen:** Factory→DW ≈ TL (~0,01 €/del/km). DW→CREP ≈ LTL (~0,03). Derfor er DW-placering kritisk for total cost.

**Reverse supply chain-processer (typisk):** product acquisition → reverse logistics → inspection/sorting → recovery → remarketing.

title: Remanufacturing — intro og workshop
body:
Remanufacturing Discovery Workshop 
Workshop idea 
You will use a real industry case to explore where value of a product remains, what 
prevents repair or remanufacturing, and what information a company needs before 
moving towards implementation. In a group (of about 4 students), you will work on one 
of the three tracks covering the organizational, technical, and economic level of 
remanufacturing. We will form groups on October 22nd. On October 29th you will 
continue the work in the same group, track, and company case. 
 
Why is the circular economy important? 
The European Union aims to double its circular material use rate by 2030 to become 
more sustainable. This rate represents the share of materials recycled and returned to 
the economy. In 2024, it reached 12.2%, with fossil materials (e.g., plastics) below the 
average at 3.8% and metal ores at 23.4%. Increasing the use of recycled materials or 
remanufactured components can reduce the environmental impacts associated with 
extraction of primary raw materials, at the same time as creating economic benefits 
for companies. 
 
Why remanufacturing? 
Circular strategies can aim to either recover materials from end-of-life components in 
a recycling process or retain product integrity and restore functionality for a new life 
cycle in a remanufacturing process. Remanufacturing can reduce energy 
consumption, material use, and the overall environmental impact. The economic value 
of a component is maintained in a new life cycle. 
 
What is remanufacturing? 
A typical remanufacturing process consists of product take-back, disassembly, 
cleaning, inspection, possible reconditioning, reassembly, and testing against current 
legislation, regulations, and the initial component properties. Restoring and verifying 
functional performance distinguish remanufacturing from direct reuse, where the 
remaining condition or lifetime may not be restored or guaranteed.  
 
What are challenges within remanufacturing? 
The implementation of remanufacturing involves challenges related to product 
condition, product and process design, take-back systems and the business case, 
environmental performance, and remanufacturing operations. 
When deploying remanufacturing efforts, a company will interact with stakeholders in 
their immediate and extended network, mostly downstream but also in upstream 
processes. They will need to create, likely new, links to be able to recover products 
and parts to be remanufactured, as well as unveil market segments willing to acquire 
remanufactured products. Therefore, an important step is to understand what aspects 
of these interactions influence their remanufacturing journey. Figure 1 shows the 
relationships among individual processes, the operational remanufacturing system, 
and the broader context of industry, regulation, and society. 
The contextual level includes regulations, industrial structures, governmental 
decisions, and societal expectations. The system level describes factors including the 
process and product design, the supply chain, individual take-back and ownership 
strategies, and the business model configuration. The process level includes individual 
operational elements that are considered, including assembly and disassembly 
operations, processing times, costs, tools, joining technologies, and reconditioning 
technologies. 
 
Figure 1: Relationship between process, system, and contextual levels 
The three levels are interdependent. Product design influences disassembly 
complexity, disassembly time, and operational costs, and subsequently affects the 
remanufacturing business case. Similarly, the take-back system and ownership are 
linked to the business model, affecting the availability of products at the end-of-life. 
Assessing the remanufacturability of a product requires system-level information on 
the supply chain linked to process-level information on technical feasibility. 
 
What are the three tracks on the workshop day? 
Track 1: Assessment of Remanufacturing Potential - Are the company and its supply 
chain ready for remanufacturing? 
This track determines whether a product is a plausible candidate for remanufacturing 
by mapping the life cycle of the product. processes and materials therein, 
stakeholders along the supply chain, also considering the availability and 
accessibility of returned products, the timing and volume of returns, as well as 
product condition. The outcome is a map of the current state of the product’s life 
cycle and its potential reverse flows, along with a prioritised list of next steps for 
analysis of remanufacturing potential. 
The key questions discussed are: 
• How much value is there to be recovered from downstream life cycle stages? 
• Are sufficient components available and accessible for remanufacturing, and 
which actors are involved in the life cycle? 
• Does the potential volume of returned products enable a feasible material flow 
for remanufacturing? 
 
Track 2: Repairability and Design Barriers - What prevents repair and 
remanufacturing? 
This track identifies product design and process barriers that hinder repair or 
remanufacturing. The analytical focus lies on the disassembly process. The output is 
a catalogue of design and process barriers, with improvement actions. 
The key questions discussed are: 
• Which components fail or require maintenance? 
• Which product design decisions make these components difficult to access? 
• Which redesign actions could improve repairability and remanufacturability? 
• Which sub-assemblies or components are time-consuming, destructive or 
difficult to disassemble? 
 
Track 3: Value Retention Opportunities - Where can repair and remanufacturing create 
value? 
This track identifies where remanufacturing may retain the product, functional, 
material, environmental, or economic value. The analysis includes the value of the 
target components, the material flow, the remanufacturing effort, take-back and 
ownership models, as well as alternative recovery strategies and business-case and 
environmental assumptions. The output is a portfolio of value-retention opportunities, 
critical assumptions, and prioritized action points. 
The key questions discussed are: 
• Where does relevant value remain over the life cycle? 
• Which components combine high residual value with feasible recovery in a 
repair or remanufacturing process?
